entry.dc:title: DEFORMATION OF A CONTACT-METAMORPHIC ROCK MASS AT LOST RIVER, ALASKA.
entry.dc:creator: Jeremic M.
entry.dc:description: The generally accepted principles of rock mechanics are used to explain the failure mechanism of a contact-metamorphic rock mass complex undergoing ellipse stress deformation. The investigation was based on structural data collected in the field and obtained from old mining and exploration reports and studies. The approach used analyzes the rock-mass mechanics resulting from a Cretaceous geological event. It follows a stress ellipse model based on the tectonic forces, the geometry of the rock structure and natural stress induced by the structural dilation. The role of geological structure and induced stress in determining the mechanism and nature of deformation bears on open-pit mining operations. Their influence on the stability of the possible open-pit mine deserves careful attention. 9 refs.

entry.dc:title: CAN ANTHRACITE MAKE A COMEBACK?
entry.dc:creator: Mutchler N.
entry.dc:description: Anthracite is overlooked or ignored by many, even as the U. S. turning once again to coal. The problem apparently occurs because it constitutes only 1 percent of U. S. coal resources. However, there are still some 17 billion tons of recoverable anthracite reserves, and this amount can be significant to a utility requiring, for instance, 1 million tons annually, or an industry requiring a fuel substitute of 200,000 tons of coal. The author takes a closer look at the anthracite potential in the U. S. , examines the anthracite's critical constraints and technology for producing methanol, and discusses massive open-pit mining.

entry.dc:title: Functional studies of the circulatory and respiratory apparatus during work in workers occupied in open-pit mining in the foothills
entry.dc:creator: Mambetaliev B.

entry.dc:title: Main Lines of Intensification of the Making of Large Open Pit Mining Machines.
entry.dc:creator: Daskovskii V.
entry.dc:description: At present, the Soviet stock of open-pit mining machinery includes rotary bucket excavators with the capacity of 5000 m**3/h and with the mass of 4850 t; walking dredgers with 100 m long jibs and with 25 m**3 buckets, with the mass of 2200 t; mechanical spades with 65 m long jibs and 35 m**3 bucket, with the mass of 2700 t; open jet excavators with 12. 5 m**3 buckets. It takes from 50 to 65 months to design and make a 2000-3000 t machine. The article considers the problem of how to speed up the designing and making of large machinery for open-pit prices in order to save costs. Examples from the assembly site at the Nikopol manganese ore mining basin are given to illustrate the problems involved.

entry.dc:title: NEW McDERMITT MINE JOINT VENTURE EMERGES AS DOMINANT FORCE IN US MERCURY PRODUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Sisselman R.
entry.dc:description: The only major mercury mine in the US is newly on stream and tuning up to achieve a designed annual throughput of 20,000 flasks of prime virgin metal by the end of 1975. Production from the McDermitt mine in Humboldt County, Nev. , should be ample to supply just under 50% of primary metal requirements of the US, which in 1974 imported 45,000 flasks and produced only 1,200. Moreover, from open-pit mining through furnacing, production will comply with strict environmental and health guidelines established by state and federal agencies. The autogenous grinding mill circuit and the furnace plant are described, as well as several departures from the norm that are evident at the McDermitt mill.

entry.dc:title: DEVELOPMENTS IN MINING MACHINERY.
entry.dc:creator: Gosnell J.
entry.dc:description: The latest innovations in underground and open-pit mining in South Africa are reviewed. These developments include the use of hydraulic rock drills in underground gold mines, the use of large rotary drilling machines in open-pit copper and iron mines, boring experiments for recovering gold ore, tests with rock-cutting machines in gold and platinum rock, the use of the impact ripping technique in collieries to excavate without explosives, underground and open-pit blasting operatiions, underground mechanized loading and dumping facilities, draglines for open-pit or strip mining, and rail haulage systems for rock transportation.

entry.dc:title: Mineralogy and origin of the Coalinga asbestos deposit
entry.dc:creator: Mumpton F.A.
entry.dc:description: Since 1960 asbestos production of the United States has more than tripled, a phenomenon due in large part to the development of the Coalinga asbestos deposit in western California. Although most asbestos ores contain 5-10 per cent chrysotile in the form of cross- or slip-fiber veins within massive serpentinite bodies, no such veins are to be found in the Coalinga deposit despite the fact that it contains more than 50 per cent recoverable chrysotile. The Coalinga ore consists of soft, powdery, pellet-like agglomerates of finely matted chrysotile surrounding blocks and fragments of serpentinite rock. The highly sheared and pulverized nature of the ore favors its exploitation by simple, open-pit mining, and high quality products can be prepared by either wet or dry milling processes. Four types of serpentine material are distinguishable: (1) hard, dense blocks of serpentinite rock, ranging from fractions of an inch to several tens of feet in diameter; (2) tough, leathery sheets, resembling mountain leather, up to several square feet in size; (3) brittle blades and plates of green serpentine, a few square inches in size; and (4) friable agglomerates of soft, powdery chrysotile containing appreciable amounts of the other three. Chrysotile is the principal component of all the above materials, with the exception of the serpentinite rock which consists mainly of lizardite and/or antigorite, with small amounts of brucite, magnetite, and very short fiber chrysotile. Although chrysotile fibers up to several microns in length are present in the leathery sheets, most Coalinga chrysotile is much shorter and arranged in a swirling mesh or disoriented, tangled fibers, much like cellulose fibers in paper. Fragments of serpentinite gangue are scattered throughout the ore and contain most of the lizardite, antigorite, and brucite. Chemical, electron probe, and X-ray analyses confirm the iron-rich nature of the brucite, a critical factor in the susceptibility of this phase to oxidation in the surface weathering zone. Here brucite either dissolves, leaving behind a residue of brown, amorphous iron oxides, or transforms in situ to pyroaurite or coalingite. Dissolved magnesium precipitates as hydromagnesite immediately above the water table throughout the deposit. The abnormally high chrysotile content of this deposit is probably a result of the intensive shearing that it underwent during or after emplacement. If the friable, chrysotile-rich ore was produced during this pulverization episode, (1) lizardite and/or antigorite in the serpentinite must have been transformed into chrysotile and (2) brucite must have been removed. It is likely that early-formed lizardite/antigorite dissolved in the ground waters which pervaded the highly sheared body and that chrysotile later precipitated from these waters, coating all available surfaces. © 1975.

entry.dc:title: Transport by Rubber Belt Conveyors at the Lignite Open-Pit Facilities in the Serbian Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (SFRJ).
entry.dc:creator: Kun J.
entry.dc:description: The author reviews the development of rubber belt conveying at the open-pit mining facilities in Serbia, which dates back to 1965. The total length of conveyor belts in lignite open-pit mining is doubling every five years, and is expected to reach about 180 km in ten years from now, which would represent a tripling over the present level. Length, speed and capacity of the conveyor belts currently in use are shown in tabular form and graphs, and the three basic transportation methods by rubber belt conveyors at the Serbian lignite open-pit mines are described.

entry.dc:title: Experts' Evaluation of the Development of the Techniques and Technology of Iron Ore Open Pit Mining in the USSR by the Year 2000.
entry.dc:creator: Shtukaturov K.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The role of experts' evaluation in compiling long-term forecasts is pointed out, the principles of composition of the questionnaries are formulated, and the mathematical tools for the treatment of answers are presented. Results of an opinion poll carried out in 1971-72 among open-pit mining and mining engineering specialists about the development of the techniques and technology of open pit iron ore mines in the USSR by the year 2000 are discussed.

entry.dc:title: New Directions of Chemical Processing of Kansk-Achinsk Basin Coal.
entry.dc:creator: Krichko A.
entry.dc:description: Conditions for open-pit mining in Kansk-Achinsk Basin in East Siberia are very favorable. It is possible to mine about 1 billion t of coal per annum by this method. The seams are up to 50-70 m thick. At present 90% of coal mined here is used locally in Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk regions. Its transportation is economically feasible only at distances well below 2000 km. The distances to the European part of the USSR where energy is required are 4,000-5,000 km, however. Therefore, several possibilities of chemical processing of Kansk-Achinsk coal for long-distance transportation are considered. One is the production of ″thermocoal″ by high-speed heating of coal to the temperature of 400-550 C in a three-stage system of vortical chambers. Another is hydrogenation together with petroleum fraction with the b. p. above 260 C. Railroad and pipeline transportation of coal products are considered.

entry.dc:title: TRENDS AND DEVELOPMENTS IN OPEN PIT MACHINERY IN THE USSR.
entry.dc:creator: Poderni R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: This paper primarily focuses on the developments in drilling and excavating equipment for open-pit mining in the USSR. A table is provided as a guide to what sizes of excavators and bore holes might be used together in a mining operation. Specifications, output and operating costs of different-size mining and quarry power shovels, as well as stripping shovels are given. A recent trend is noted toward equipping large surface mines with draglines instead of shovels.

entry.dc:title: TRENDS AND DEVELOPMENTS IN OPENCAST DRILLING AND BLASTING.
entry.dc:creator: Bauer A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The author reviews various methods, equipment and explosives used in drilling and blasting by the open-pit mining method, and explores such vital factors as productivity, drilling costs, bulk strengths for different slurries and dry mixs, as well as velocity of detonation. The trend toward ever-larger drills with incresed pulldown weight is noted. Three classes of explosives used for blasting in open-pit mining are described in detail, as well as priming practice and more effective ways of fragmentation.

entry.dc:title: ROTARY DRILLING WITH AUTOMATED CONTROLS - NEW FORCE IN OPEN-PIT BLASTHOLE PRODUCTION.
entry.dc:creator: Li T.
entry.dc:description: Automation of large diameter rotary drills, one of the latest major innovations by United States drill manufacturers, is among the most sophisticated applications of solid-state technology for the rugged open-pit mining by most users has been slow and has yet to significantly affect the rapidly rising costs of mining and stripping. Three United States manufacturers - Bucyrus-Erie Co, Gardner Denver Co, and Marin Power Shovel Co. - have all committed a large part of recent research and development capital to production rotary drills with automated controls. Such development at present is limited to the largest of the manufacturer's rotary drill lines, capable of producing 9 7/8- to 17-in. -diam blastholes. These drills can reportedly meet today's heavy demand for increased open-pit productivity in face of a growing shortage of skilled manpower. Paper describes the automated drilling controls as designed by the above listed manufacturers and gives their specifications.

entry.dc:title: Problem of Accounting for Attenuation of Vibrations of Jib Structures in Open-Pit Mining Machines.
entry.dc:creator: Lynskii L.
entry.dc:description: A method is proposed for determining the members which take into account attenuation of the vibrations of jibs. Taking spreaders as an example, engineering formulas are derived for calculating the coefficients determining damping in the dynamic systems of jib structures.

entry.dc:title: Classification of Technico-Economic Tasks of Open-Pit Mining for Computer-Aided Solution.
entry.dc:creator: Khokhryakov V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The proposed classification involves division of problems into four types: technical geometric, economic and technico-economic. The latter are subdivided in accordance with the exactness of the solution, the level and scale of the project, the contents and methods of solving the problem, the length of the estimated period, the form of presentation of the geological and technological information, differences of expenditure and comparability of the useful effect. The classes of project design, planning, and management, the subclasses of approximate and detailed solutions, the groups of problems of particular branches of industry, regions, dressing combines, and open-pit mines, the subgroups of distribution, mining and geological, and technological problems, and other, narrower subdivisions are single out. The main technico-economic tasks of open-pit mining are enumerated.

entry.dc:title: Development of the Methods of Determination of Productivity of Open-Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Arsent'ev A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The case of maximum-intensity open-pit mining both in depth and in horizontal direction with a variable slope of the working edge is considered and the possible productivity of the mine is determined in the following way. First, the rational direction of the development of the extraction work in the open-pit mine is determined. Then the layout of the mining work for each level is constructed in accordance with two variants: that of maximum mineral extraction and of ensuring a minimum working area. The minimum time of level preparation is determined by means of graphs or analytical dependences. The volumes of ore extracted from the mine during the preparation of each level is calculated. The graphs of the growing volumes of the mineral in time are constructed and a curve of stabilized productivity is drawn. Its sector that has the greatest angle of inclination to the X-coordinate corresponds to the productivity of the mine that is the maximum possible for the given conditions.

entry.dc:title: Verification of Long-Term Forecasts of Tehcnico-Economic Indices of Open-Pit Workings by the Methods of the Statistical Theory of Prediction.
entry.dc:creator: Eremina V.I.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The statistical theory of prediction develops quantitative methods of forecasting and the ways to improve their accuracy. Forecasting is accomplished by different methods of extrapolation of time series. Under the conditions of the statistical theory of prediction verification of the forecasts is carried out by confirming each forecast by the prediction methods. Three statistical methods of calculation of the prospects for future dynamics are proposed for long-term forecasting of technico-economic indices of open-pit mining works. These are: the method of direct extrapolation of the forecast trend, exponential smoothing in accordance with Brown and adaptive smoothing by Laguerre polynomials.

entry.dc:title: CONSIDERATION OF SOME FACTORS AFFECTING THE ECONOMIC USE OF WIRE ROPE ON OPEN-PIT MINING EQUIPMENT.
entry.dc:creator: Finnis P.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes the use of wire rope on open-pit mining equipment, giving specifications and examples of the performance achieved. Installation methods are also discussed, making the paper of considerable practical use to mine operators.

entry.dc:title: HEAT FLOW AND PERMAFROST.
entry.dc:creator: Jessop A.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the distribution of frozen ground in the zone of discontinuous permafrost in relation to the pattern of surface temperature. The importance of understanding permafrost in relation to surface construction and open-pit mining operations is stressed.

entry.dc:title: THE WAY THE MONEY GOES IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: While the operating costs in surface mining operations can vary from as little as 17 to over 130 cents/ton, it is possible to determine meaningful figures for industry as a whole. Article presents a summary that outlines the broad cost patterns for the major functions within open pit operations and gives overall estimates for both operating and capital expenditure.

entry.dc:title: ELECTRIC MINING SHOVEL AS A PRIMARY DIGGING TOOL FOR OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Cherones W.
entry.dc:description: This paper describes the history of the development and application of the electric mining shovel in open-pit mining, dealing particularly with far-reaching advancements in three primary areas: metallurgy, mechanical design and electrical systems. Hoist drives and crowd drives including the Magnetorque and Electrotorque systems, and the integral propel drive are given close attention.

entry.dc:title: MINING AND PETROLEUM TECHNOLOGY. PROC OF THE NINTH COMMONWEALTH MINING AND METALLURGICAL CONGRESS 1969, V 1, MAY 3-24 1969, LONDON, ENGL
entry.dc:creator: JONES ED MJ
entry.dc:description: The papers of mining in this volume cover a wide variety of minerals and metals and methods of extraction. In particular there are papers on the application of modern techniques and mechanization in the mining of coal, gold, copper diamonds, lead, silver, zinc, and tin, coverage being given to deep mining, open-pit mining, beach mining, and dredging. Two papers are concerned with the sinking of shafts; one describes methods of pregrouting shaft sites to prevent inrushes of water during sinking operatins, and the other describes the shaft sinking techniquesused in sinking the potash shafts at Saskatchewan. The papers dealing with petroleum cover a wide range of technology relating to the offshore production of liquid petroleum and natural gas. They deal particularly with offshore drilling, the production facilities, and the construction and operation of the necessary pipe lines.

entry.dc:title: BELT CONVEYOR SYSTEMS USED ON PTOLEMAIS OPEN-PIT MINING SITE, GREECE,
entry.dc:creator: KULLIK E
entry.dc:description: Development of open-cast mining operations, present system and mechanical equipment of the belt conveyor systems of an open-pit mining site converted from combination power shovel, scraper and truck operations to belt conveyor operations. Five bucket-wheel excavators are employed for breaking up and reclaiming materials. In 1969 6 million t of coal were produced, 30% more than originally scheduled. The overburden which varies from sharp-edged rock to sludge and paste presents special difficulties.

entry.dc:title: OPEN-PIT DEWATERING AT PINE POINT MINES
entry.dc:creator: CALVER B
entry.dc:description: As open pit operations expanded at Pine Point, hydraulic aquifer evaluation was undertaken to establish the criteria necessary for the design of a feasible dewatering system. The extreme climate of this northern location dictated that the ore zone under extraction be rendered as dry as possible to minimize freezing effects. The design and implementation of such a system necessitated detailed hydraulic evaluation and the problems that occurred are typical of those inherent in open-pit mining operations in northernreas. The hydrological analysis used in solution of problem is simple and readily applicable to most open-pit dewatering problems.

entry.dc:title: MAINTENANCE OF LARGE SHOVESL IN OPEN-PIT MINING AT QUEBEC CARTIER
entry.dc:creator: PROULX GP
entry.dc:description: Quebec Cartier Mining Company operates ten 8-cu yd electric shovels to extract iron ore from its open-pit mine in northern Quebec, where the temperature has averaged 27 F during the past 9 yr. Experience gained since the start of operations in 1959 has shown the need for sound equipment specifications designed to meet the existing mining conditions along with constant training of manpower and engineering assistance to improve operating costs and equipment availability.
